page: Microsoft Azure E64ds_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the EDSv5 family, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. The processor includes a 48 MB L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX-512, including AVX512_VNNI, and cryptography standards like AES and SHA_NI. The server is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, and includes 2458 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability.

In benchmark evaluations, the E64ds_v5 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory performance is also robust, with large-block uncached read and write bandwidths placing in the top tier. Database operations and key-value store performance are notable, as evidenced by strong results in Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations, which reached 61.58 million operations per second. However, single-core performance metrics, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores, remain in the middle 50% average tier.

The server exhibits clear resource density advantages for memory-bound and storage-intensive workloads, offering a high memory-to-core ratio and substantial local storage. This hardware profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale databases and memory-intensive enterprise applications by reducing the need to scale out to more nodes. A key performance tradeoff is observed in large-scale machine learning tasks; while prompt processing for a 70B LLM model falls in the average tier, text generation for the same model is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Consequently, this server is appropriate for relational databases, in-memory caching, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
